title: Chat Moderation
body: The game itself is fine. The main chat, however, is a completely different story. For a game that children can access, the lack of effective chat moderation is honestly concerning. Players are allowed to openly sexualize things and have blatantly inappropriate conversations in main chat. Even worse, I’ve watched the chat get bombarded with disturbing conversations involving children. How is this allowed to continue in a public chat? The censorship system makes even less sense. Completely harmless words get censored while genuinely inappropriate conversations somehow make it through. What exactly is the filter protecting players from at that point? Having a word filter is not the same thing as actually moderating a community. If children can access this game, the developers need to take responsibility for monitoring public chat, reviewing reports, and actually enforcing their rules. Sword x Staff can be enjoyable, but the current state of main chat is unacceptable. Stop censoring random harmless words while allowing conversations that actually deserve moderation to remain visible. Protect your younger players and fix the chat system.

title: This game is boring
body: I have played this game for a couple months and quit the game. This game gives the illusion that it’s for free to play or for those that spend low amounts of money on a game. You can create dishes to earn dawnium but players will stop buying them from trading post later in game. This is an idle/gacha game which has players slowly progress unless you spend loads of money on it. Gameplay progress is slow, the amount of time I have played this game per day is 1 hour or less. Dungeons attempts are limited per day. You’re limited on how many resources you can gather at the max of 300 stamina which is hardly enough to progress. Clearing areas can be difficult unless you spend money on the game. Each new dungeon becomes harder to clear which in result has you not clear the difficulty each one has to offer when a new dungeon unlocks every 2 weeks. You do not get enough shards in time unless you’re a big spender and do the hardest difficulty each time a new dungeon unlocks. Relics do help increase your power but you’ll have to spend a lot to get more power. The lucky statue is a relic that helps increase your chance of getting a gear drop or double shards when each gear requires 100 shards to craft, but it has barely helped me in inquiring gear or double shard drops. You can get gear that is required for your class from auction house but it comes at a price of spending $100 or more depending how much a pack of luminium is, then the gear will be replaced once you do the next dungeon that has higher power gear. Which will have you spend even more money. You can get divine craft stone to re-roll certain stats but it is only by luck to get the stats you want which can cost a lot of divine craft stone if you’re one of the unlucky ones. The only way to get xp is by unlocking statues that gives idle experience, which you have to wait from hours to a day. Tournaments and arena have become boring because of players that spend a lot on the game. They always get the better rewards that you receive from them. I can never get into nexus tournament because the same 4 players team up in each team and get in the top 8 which leaves the rest of us which, as in hundreds or less players depending on server unable to compete and get the chance of getting the outfits from it and divine craft stone. Gems are have become harder to upgrade. You barely get enough gems from whaleback island,split mirage, sky tower and loong haven. The gems have a chance to fail to increase the tier. Events don’t even give enough rewards to progress and power up in game. We don’t even get an event to get gems. This game is not for free to play or people who spend little amounts on a game. This is my full review of the game.

title: God awful, mind numbing game
body: I preordered this game when I saw it on the App Store. I didn't quite expect a masterpiece, so my standards for this game were low. Somehow, this game even failed to reach that mark. This game is the definition of pointless. Everything is a numbers game. It’s one of those awful types of games where all you do is continuously upgrade your stuff so that you can watch a big number grow even bigger. Mind numbing slop at its finest. One of the things that made me quit this game in under a week were the ridiculous ads they started putting out after the game launched. It’s blatant false advertising much like how other slop games advertise themselves. Some defenders may try to say “but the developers don’t control or make the ads.” Sure, but there’s a thing called quality control. Clearly the developers are content that these misleading ads are getting people to download the game. They know they COULD do better, they just choose not to, and instead fake their work. Pathetic. For actual gameplay, there’s essentially almost none. It’s all an illusion of progress. You wander around a meaningless world with meaningless characters in it. You’ll find yourself quickly being gated by enemies with power levels much higher than your own, forcing you to upgrade your gear. You’ll probably spend more time in menus managing your trash than actually doing anything. After upgrading things, you’ll inevitably run out of materials, forcing you to AFK for resources. THAT’S NOT GAMEPLAY. I honestly don’t know which is worse for the illusion of gameplay: grinding or AFK nonsense. I don’t even know why this game calls itself a “third way RPG” (what does that even mean lol???), it’s just gachaslop that’ll EOS in less than 5 years. The gacha in this game isn’t too bad, I guess (though I’ve heard in that in a recent collab event they were already getting P2W with that). You gamble for skills, pets, or relics. Boring stuff like that. This game feels very lifeless. I wouldn’t even be surprised if some of the players on the leaderboard are just bots created by the developers. I can’t imagine anyone actually spending thousands of dollars on this trash game. The story and characters are similarly lifeless. They are bland and exist solely to drive you through one land so you can move onto the next. Character designs are painfully generic too. The voice acting is obnoxious or highly questionable at best. If you’d like to keep your brain cells, don’t even give this game a chance.

This is when nobody else is in the area for a solid hour and I am consistently waiting 5-15 minutes before I can queue up with others to do dungeons and bosses. They time-gate your progression and make you wait before you can move to the next ranking. They also prevent you from cancelling a run or booting another player when they are trolling and wasting the entire preparation period before letting the party get disbanded due to auto-timer. This makes runs frustrating rather than exciting, and I often dread having to do any co-op activities for rewards. The in-game chat is fine, but I want an option to prevent private messages either forever or for a set period of time, unless it is from a friend or guild mate. I would also like an option to go into low-level dungeons by myself instead of constantly waiting for someone to join me. If I can't progress, then at least let me farm by myself for a bit before I have to AFK and wait again. And for the record, you can't choose to be a goblin or imp or whatever and get pros and cons. title: Pay to Win / Odd Timegating
body: There's a functional dopamine loop here, and that's about the nicest thing I can say. While I don’t mind paying for skins or additional content, everything else feels engineered to separate you from your wallet, not to make a good game. Pay-to-win isn't a feature, it's the foundation. Limited-time offers, premium advancement tracks, it's relentless. This isn't monetization bolted onto a game; the game was built around the monetization. And don’t forget the ranking system, it’s like look at this person, they spent and absolute ****ton of cash. The story is an afterthought. "Chaos exists, get ‘er <adventurer>" is genuinely the entire narrative. Clearing a zone gives you nothing, no weight, no payoff. And they couldn't even leave exploration alone… 100% completion is locked behind unique keys, which are locked behind purchases, which may even be locked until you get to the next zone. Companions are a rough draft. The visage leveling system had potential, but the dialogue reads like it skipped both translation and editing. It’s distracting in a bad way. Will I continue? Probably not. The flashy combos were interesting at first, but the shine is wearing off and there really isn’t anything to keep you there.

Like yeah they get limited titles with poor rewards but they are really worth it. It kinda makes the top players decide to do what they got to do and get off for the day. title: Extremely p2w 🥵
body: Don’t download this game unless you’re prepared to spend $70+ every month. This game is a breeding ground for FOMO and frustration. At first, it seems incredibly fun: cute graphics, a storyline, different progression paths, and tons of things to do. But eventually, you reach a point where you can’t clear dungeons without help from whales — and they often ignore you. Forget about competing in cross-server tournaments. The rewards might as well not exist for you, either. You can’t take a break and come back without running into problems, even with the 14-day comeback support. You’ll fall behind everyone else and end up ruining your account. I’m currently in Season 3, and I’m exhausted. I’ve read tons of guides on how to play this game efficiently, and even with all that knowledge, the best I can manage is around Top 15 in the Arena and Top 16 in the Tournament. But the worst part is that if you start playing now, you’ll have already missed out on half the events. Many costumes and bonuses will be permanently out of your reach. And don’t expect one big, open world to explore, either. This game is designed to drain your wallet. Yes, there are F2P players, but even they tend to achieve slightly less than I have — and they do it by constantly going without things they want and sticking to a strict routine! But seriously, it’s a game! It’s supposed to be fun, not turn into a second job that eats your life. You’re expected to be online when new servers open, rush through every location before everyone else, and grind for XP as fast as possible just to get a temporary power advantage. A beautiful, cute, and engaging game is being ruined by outrageous pay-to-win monetization. Competing with your wallets is a game for the very rich. If you don’t care about PvP or tournaments and can tolerate constantly running short on resources and having very little variety in what you can do, then go ahead and enjoy the game as a F2P player. Though that enjoyment probably won’t last long.

title: Great experiences, needs some little improvements.
body: I’ve read the comments, and I’m actively playing the game. I think the classes were well designed, but with every season the differences between them become more noticeable, especially in terms of disadvantages. The rankings already show the reality of the game: the top players are mostly P2W, which is understandable…if you spend money, that’s part of the benefit. However, the developers should test PvP between classes using similar levels and stats. The gap in performance between some classes is huge, and this also affects PvE progression. Exploration also has too many restrictions: level requirements, rank, damage requirements, keys, special tools, etc. It’s frustrating to know that in 24 hours I’ll finally unlock the next area, only to realize that I’m already much stronger than the recommended level and then have to wait another 24 hours for the next one. Progression should be based more on level ranges and offer several areas at the same time. Otherwise, the game becomes repetitive. I also thought buying some items would improve my experience, but honestly, it didn’t make much difference. I understand that it’s impossible to satisfy everyone, but there are definitely things that could be improved. Events are another example. Some have unique rewards, but the dance event felt like spending time just to collect a few notes. The recent minigames have been more entertaining, though. The whale event was especially confusing because there was no real introduction or explanation of the collaboration. Not everyone playing the game knows anime or shows from other countries. Even a short introduction explaining what the whale is and why we are fighting it would help a lot. Right now, I’m sure many players are just hunting it for the special coins without even knowing what the whale represents. Overall, I like the game, but I think improving class balance, exploration progression, and event explanations would make the experience much better.

title: So Much Potential, Unfortunately Buried Under P2W
body: This game has so much potential. It genuinely feels like playing an MMO on your phone, and there are a lot of things here that I really enjoy. Unfortunately, the longer I play, the more obvious it becomes where this game seems to be headed. The Good Character customization The character customization is actually really cool and surprisingly unique. There are a lot of ways to make your character feel like your own. Skills and class variety Each class has numerous skills, and the order in which you use them actually matters. There is some real depth to combat, and I like that different classes can fill traditional MMO roles. Collectible outfits The different outfits are a fun addition and give you another way to customize your character. Characters, story, and voice acting I was honestly surprised by this. The characters and story aren’t bad at all, and the voice acting is actually pretty good. It makes the world feel more like a real MMO rather than just another mobile game. Tank / Healer / DPS roles You can actually build traditional MMO parties with tanks, healers, and DPS. That’s something I really appreciate because it gives the game more of that classic MMO feeling. Dungeons and boss fights Being able to run dungeons and fight bosses with actual players is great. These are some of the moments where the game really feels like a legitimate MMO on your phone. Pets They’re cute. That’s pretty much it. Arena The Arena is decent and adds another thing to do. Auction House The fact that there is an actual Auction House is a HUGE positive. This could have been one of the features that really sets this game apart from other mobile MMOs. Unfortunately, there’s a pretty major problem with it, which brings me to the bad. The Bad You guessed it: It’s P2W. Heavily. There are numerous progression paths that are blocked by vines, stone pillars, and other obstacles. Yes, you can remove them using items that are technically obtainable for free, but those items cost an absolute fortune. And there are WAY too many of these obstacles. I’m currently looking at 12 different paths on my map that I can’t access because I don’t have the required items. It’s incredibly frustrating to look at all of these areas and know that I can’t reasonably access them without spending a ridiculous amount of resources. Exploration should make you excited to see what’s around the next corner. Instead, I’m constantly running into another obstacle and thinking, “Well, I guess I’m not going there.” The Auction House This could have been a feature that genuinely sets this game apart. But, of course, the only currency you can use in the Auction House is premium currency. So essentially, you’re buying and trading items using real-money currency. And that creates a situation where whales can dominate the entire market and continue pulling further and further ahead. If you’re F2P—or even close to it—the Auction House might as well not exist for you. It’s essentially a marketplace for whales to trade with other whales. SO. MANY. THINGS. TO. BUY. The game constantly pushes purchases at you. There is FOMO everywhere, and it feels extremely predatory. Like most games in this genre, you’re eventually going to hit walls. Maybe you need more power. Maybe you need a certain item. Maybe you’re blocked from progressing somewhere. And then, conveniently… “For only $5.99, you can get just enough power to move forward!” Big surprise. The problem isn’t that the game has things you can buy. I’m completely fine with games making money. The problem is that the game seems to constantly create obstacles and then present spending money as the solution. Conclusion This is the frustrating part: I genuinely think this game could be incredible. There is something special here. The MMO mechanics, classes, customization, dungeons, parties, skills, story, and overall presentation have a ton of potential. If this game were subscription-based, I honestly think I’d have a hard time putting it down. I know this will probably fall on deaf ears, but the F2P community really needs a win. Give us a subscription option. Create separate servers for whales and F2P players. Reduce the paywalls. Make the Auction House usable without premium currency. Give players a reasonable way to explore and progress without constantly feeling like they’re being pushed toward the cash shop. Do something. Because the foundation of this game is genuinely good. I don’t want to see another game with this much potential turn into another mobile cash shop with an MMO attached to it. You guys have something special here. Please don’t bury it under monetization.

title: A good game with room for improvement
body: I wrote a review before but after playing to the end of the fourth area and trying all the classes I decided to write an updated one. While I like the game and it’s fun the class balance issues are a big problem. There are four classes and their name changes after each upgrade. There is a tank class, a melee dps, a magic dps and a healer class. Unfortunately the magic dps class is so much better than the others that it’s by far the most played. The dps magic class gets every element except darkness , the most damage dealing potential the most class synergy and versatility. The others classes just can’t compete with it. The healer class gets healing and support spells and darkness element for decent damage. They also get some summon pet abilities but the pets die so fast and don’t do much damage so they are useless. The healer class is decent but very boring to play and you don’t see many. The tank class has water and light elements and some tanking and physical skills. They don’t really become good at tanking until they get the passive ability to reduce damage from taunted enemies late into the game. The tank class is probably the worst in the game. While it can draw aggro the class isn’t very durable for what it’s supposed to do and their armor gets punched through by bosses like it’s made of paper. It also has the lowest dps in the game making it subpar in every way. The melee dps has fire and darkness elements and physical skills and is somewhere in between the tank and magic dps class. They don’t have taunt but are very hard to kill with skills like indomitable will which is just a much better version of the self revive skill the actual tank has. They also have some passive abilities that make them stronger as they lose health both offensively and defensively making the tank class almost obsolete. The only downside is they don’t have a lot of synergy with their passive abilities so it can be hard to build a good skill set with them. The other aspect of character strategy is the fantomon. Once you grow them into an adult it is like having a second character. While they are my favorite part of the game they could use some rebalancing. You hardly ever see any used except the two mystic rarity ones. The others could definitely use some buffs to make them more competitive and useful in combat. The only other gripe I have with the game is how little effort is put into your own character’s appearance. You can customize the costume and look of them but the portrait of them is always the default white hair and red eyes with a different color background based on your class. You don’t even get to use any of the outfits you get from dungeons because the developers want to sell you costumes for real money. It’s a shame considering the developers try to use attractive female characters to sale the game in the ads you see for it. The npcs look well drawn so I don’t see why the one you will play as for 100s of hours potential can’t have the portrait be more personalized.

body: You get exp points from just waiting is nice, a lot of helping out each other and straight forward mechanics for dungeons and battles. And these auction can go easy as $50 per equipment, and new area weapons right now are $300 US per weapon/equipment. And these dungeons you can only dive 2 times a day for free to play and collect random drops and guaranteed equipment shards (100 needed to complete 1 equipment). title: almost perfect
body: I really, really wanna give this game five stars. It's genuinely really fun. It's got really intuitive gameplay, really good voice acting for all the characters, and just overall avoids a bunch of the problems I've personally had with other RPG mobile games in the past. It's been a near daily play for me, and I'm at around 11.4M power. The enemy designs are genuinely fantastic, and I like the NPC's and settings a ton. I'm very interested to see where the story goes from here!! My biggest issue personally? I'm pretty sure there's AI being used in event art. The recent Hot Pot event seemed like the splash art was at least modified with AI (especially in the pot itself) and looking back on the Zeus event, and the art puzzle minigames from another prior event make me worry that we're throwing in the towel for these smaller events. Even this most recent halloween event seems to be using it for backgrounds, and unfortunately, it's making me suspicious of more front and center art, such as the little witch ghosts featured in the current event. Now, to be fair to the dev team, I get art takes a long time and they are probably on a tight schedule/budget, and I applaud them for not allowing it to be used in the creation of the mainline story and character designs, at least as far as I can tell. But, as a player and a visual artist, I can confidently say that AI will always impede with the final result of a game's visual identity. It's just a side effect of what AI actually is, which is, in very simple terms, a pattern recognition machine. Certainly, it's gotten advanced, but it will likely never be able to fine-tune to a unique/original artistic vision the way a human can. Overall, it makes the final result feel cheaper and removes that feeling of deep care, respect for the medium, and consideration to player experience that I see in most of the rest of the game. While I know my comment probably won't do much to change these decisions as they are made, I do hope the devs keep their AI use to a minimum if possible--It's very appealing to go for the easy or cheap option, but ultimately I think that choice is a sacrifice, especially when it comes to art and storytelling. Thank you to the devs for working so hard to make this game, I really do enjoy it!!

title: Intrigued me and didn’t disappoint
body: I’ve played games like this before. For this kind of game it is really enjoyable. The audio and visuals are relaxing and progression feels consistent and rewarding. There are in game purchases but not under pressure. People who get into this type of game are likely to buy in game purchases simply because they enjoy the game a lot and play daily. But for others who are playing more casual it never feels like you HAVE to do anything. There are no ads. The characters are cute, the menus and dialogue, UI, and spells and abilities are also well done with quality. The mini games and scenarios you play through for leveling are light and fun, the AFK rewards feel rewarding. I like this game overall. My gaming background is Blizzard and Bethesda. I think this game has the feeling of an MMO minimized. Ample choices, customization, teamwork and ability to openly socialize. It’s a fun mobile game.

title: Read This First!!
body: Try this game if: You want a fantasy idle RPG that respects your time, lets you swap roles freely, and treats skill collection (rather than character collection) as the gacha hook. The KonoSuba launch collab is the largest free-pull window the game has shown, which makes the first two weeks the cheapest entry point you will ever get. F2P-friendly if you follow the standard hoard rules. Hold off if: You bounce off idle systems or want hard-mode active combat from day one. About 50% of players quit before the end of the Verdantglade, which is the design intent: Boltray treats the first map as a filter. If you would rather a game prove itself in the first hour than gate its real systems behind two weeks of progression, this is the wrong genre for you.

title: So close
body: I LOVE this game. But the hard progression locks, in-game shops, and pass rewards are severely lackluster. Areas are level locked, but sometimes you can’t rank up for a while on account of it being on “cooldown” for 2+ days, and that’s only if you get enough EXP by then to level up. Theres no way to get EXP (real amounts) unless you wait for a while. OTHER areas are locked until you can purchase items from specific shops, and those take several days to save up for, with very minimal rewards after unlocking. That’s a huge issue imo. The guild and other mini shops are pretty disappointing and never have enough supplies. Purchase limit is incredibly small with, once again, several days of cooldown. I’m not f2p, but don’t spend a ton. The passes I don’t feel are actually super beneficial to growth as most of the time it adds up to a few days of collecting items, plus a couple more rare items (that unlock the mini areas) Aside from those issues, the gameplay is super fun and isn’t a time-trap. I’m sticking it out to see if things get resolved because it is a genuinely good game. Pretty easy progression with some hard locks and iffy shops/passes, but that doesn’t break it for me. Boss fights are challenging, progression is satisfying, and watching your character grow from weak to unbelievably powerful never gets old. The world is beautiful, the soundtrack is great, and the idle mechanics respect your time without taking away from active gameplay. Whether you want to grind, theorycraft, or just explore, there’s something here for you. No game is perfect, but the developers have built an RPG with real depth and tons of potential. If they continue adding classes, skills, raids, and endgame content, this could become one of the best mobile MMORPGs on the market. 10/10. title: Awesome game!
body: I have been enjoying this game for a month or so. It’s amazing. The art is adorable. There are so many things to do each day to level. The guild and grouping set up is so great. I actually interact with people because the game is designed to be played with others. It feels like a MMO on my phone, which is awesome. The dungeons are basically automatic, so it’s been nice to go into a dungeon while I’m doing work on the computer or whatever else I’m doing. And if you do have to alt-tab out of the game, you still get all your loot. Hopefully you don’t let your team down by not healing yourself or something, but it’s really not annoying if people do. You get 4 dungeon rewards a day, but it’s dependent on people queueing, and since I’m studying on a laptop, I just constantly queue. There are no ads. So great. But that means we need to pay them for their work other ways. Therefore, this is the first app I actually make purchases from. My first purchase was great - I bought it and instantly got it. Last week Apple notified me of a charge by them I didn’t purchase. I didn’t notice items in my account, as I may have left the $15 charge if I did get stuff. There was no way to know what it was for or ask about it, so I refused the charge… and was auto banned. ☹️ I took screenshots of my account and the charge. It took a day, but they lifted it as soon as they got the information. I bet people are trying to steal from them, and they’re already not getting money from ads. That’s terrible. You definitely do not have make any purchases to stay in the top 5% of players if you’re farming your daily stuff, but this game is absolutely worth giving some extra money to for all their hard work and their lovely mmo they have developed for us. Also, their customer service is great.

title: Finally, a perfect AFK
body: I’ve been playing this game for about a month, and I am completely hooked. First off, the system is set so you will level up whether you’re actively logged in or not. Most games of this type in my experience that label themselves ‘AFK’ may collect resources while you are logged out, and I can’t think of any that actually give you experience points without paying for a pass or auto-gatherer. Not so with S&S - it’s a pleasure to open your game and discover your character has leveled up while you were away. Another really nice feature is you can change your class, and keep your levels. No more multiple accounts just to try them all! I have also enjoyed the crossover events; the mini games are great, and you can collect outfits, hairstyles, and weapons without spending a ridiculous amount. In fact, I’m amazed that this is a free-to-play game with NO ADS. The rewards are very generous, and you can get surprisingly far without spending anything. (Do spend a little, they truly deserve it). But I think the biggest pull for me is the graphics & design quality. Spend a little time on the Home screen, just to watch shooting stars and fireflies. Look for the shadows of whales swimming overhead in Aqualis battles. The entire game is polished and it’s obvious that care went into the world crafting. Gameplay is easy to pick up, and addictive enough to keep you coming back for more. So, my message to the devs: you have created a game that’s just what I was looking for, except I didn’t know it until I played it. Thank you for making such a fantastic, beautiful world to explore!

title: So much fun!
body: For starters i’m mostly F2P, and never feel like I’ve hit a paywall. I started playing on day one and have been excited to login everyday! SXS feels a lot like triple A MMOs with its competitive guild community while also having a strong community that hasn’t failed to help lower players through content. The Idle/AFK part is great too and makes progression steady without stressing about time management and strict login times. The Devs have been great on delivering new content for all types of players and engaging with the community as well. They have a dedicated live support team to answer questions and resolve issues fast. Overall SwordXStaff has been so much fun in the first month and have been recommending it to all my friends. 10/10 Game and Community!

title: A well designed game!
body: First review I’ve ever written. SxS has truly developed a remarkable game. I’ve played so many mobile rpgs and usually quit within the first few hours, if not sooner. The character progression in this game is balanced, capped to an extent that people can’t get too far ahead unless they bit spend (which some do), but that’s okay. The daily runs, leveling, arena and character individuality this game brings is fantastic. The micro transactions aren’t crazy, and the lack of pressure to spend is great. So far, the community takes the cake. Friendly, engaging and always willing to help. 5/5 game that I will play for the foreseeable future.
